batch_node.name: teleport page v0.2.0
batch_node.description: The /teleport operator page (req-teleport-page): the deployment graph panel with its projection, elevation, layout (teleport-deployment.js) and twelve scene searches — one per node set and one per edge type drawn — and seven teleport-board panels (posture, roles, identity, resources, requests, machines, trust). Reusable: nothing here names an instance; every search takes the cluster's name (?cluster=<cluster name>) and, absent, every cluster. References no entity outside this file.

node.name: Teleport
node.description: The operator's front page for one Teleport cluster in a FedRAMP 20x environment: the deployment picture on top (control plane, storage, keys, agents and what they protect), then the cluster's posture, roles and grants, sign-in, protected resources, access requests, machine identities and trust. ?cluster=<cluster name> picks the cluster by its name (its natural key), matched exactly; with one cluster on the grid it is chosen. Design nodes (dcom=design) render like observed ones and the board marks them.

node.name: Teleport deployment
node.description: One cluster's deployment as a placed picture (teleport-deployment.js): proxies and auth servers inside the cluster box with the certificate authorities, what each runs on to the left, the keys the CAs sign with to the right, the state, audit and recording stores beneath, then each agent with the resources it serves and the targets those front. Scene searches name every edge type they draw.

node.name: teleport deployment projection
node.description: Icon-badge chrome (each node's type icon at its upper-left), one elevation running the teleport deployment layout; a placed picture (lock_nodes) opened fitted.

node.name: teleport deployment elevation
node.description: One Teleport cluster's deployment at one elevation.

definition.description: One Teleport cluster's deployment at one elevation.

node.name: teleport deployment layout
node.description: Scopes the scene to one cluster (the cluster named by the ?cluster= input, else the only one), nests proxies, auth servers and CAs in the cluster box by their BELONGS_TO_CLUSTER edges, then places compute, keys, storage, agents, resources and targets in bands relative to what they attach to. Names no instance; a node no band accounts for is drawn under the picture and reported.

node.name: teleport — clusters
node.description: The chosen cluster (?cluster=<cluster name>), or every Teleport cluster on the grid when ?cluster is absent, so a cluster with nothing attached is still drawn and, with several, the picker can be drawn. Scene rule: when the deployment picture gains a node or edge type, its search is added here — the graph draws only edges some search returns.

cluster.description: The Teleport cluster's name (teleport__teleport_cluster.name, its natural key), from ?cluster= on the page, matched exactly. Absent, the default is the sentinel 'teleport__teleport_cluster' (the cluster type's own slug), which every cluster's entity_type equals, so every cluster matches: the one cluster on a single-cluster grid. The sentinel stands in for the optional filter Gryphon cannot yet say directly (tap#360); the cluster model refuses that name, so the sentinel is never a cluster's name.

Scene rule: when the deployment picture gains a node or edge type, its search is added here — the graph draws only edges some search returns.

node.name: Cluster posture
node.description: The cluster's FedRAMP 20x-relevant settings — FIPS build, signature suite, local auth, second factor, device trust, session recording — each marked against the expectation it serves, then what the cluster holds. Grey means not observed: the grid has no value, which is neither a pass nor a fail.
